extracted.intended_audience: teachers, educators, and community members interested in First Nations/Indigenous storytelling and pedagogy (particularly K–12 and informal educators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for teaching, performing, and preparing First Nations oral stories in classroom and community settings, emphasizing cultural protocols, performance technique, and listener engagement. Includes resources and prompts for adapting stories into learning activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story types and purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories can vary from the sacred to the historical. Some focus on social, political, and cultural ways. Some are entertaining, even humorous. Some tell of personal, family, community or an entire nation’s experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the range of purposes a story may serve (teaching, entertainment, history, cultural explanation) and select or present stories appropriate to the learning goal and audience sensitivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural ownership and permission
rubrics_metrics.description: Some are 'owned' by certain clans or families and can only be told by a member of that group. Others can be told by anyone who knows them and cares for them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether a story is clan- or family-owned and follow community protocols; obtain permission and defer to cultural authority when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stories as cultural expression and context
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories reflect the perceptions, relationships, beliefs and attitudes of a particular people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat stories as carriers of cultural knowledge and worldview; provide contextual framing so listeners understand cultural meanings and relations embedded in the tale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance: voice, vocal expression, and intonation
rubrics_metrics.description: First Nations storytelling involves expert use of the voice, vocal and body expression, intonation...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage listeners through voice fluctuations and expressiveness; consider how to apply similar voice inflections in classroom storytelling to animate characters and convey tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance: body language and facial animation
rubrics_metrics.description: First Nations storytelling involves... facial animation, [and] body expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate facial expressions and body movements to support the narrative — mindful of cultural norms — to help listeners visualize and emotionally connect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of verbal imagery and visualization
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of verbal imagery... listening encompasses visualizing the characters and their actions and letting the emotions surface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ vivid verbal imagery to prompt listeners' visualization; encourage listeners to 'listen with three ears' (two on the head and one in the heart) to deepen engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative craft: plot and character development
rubrics_metrics.description: First Nations storytelling involves... context, plot and character development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop clear narrative arcs and character portrayals appropriate to oral delivery; emphasize actions and relationships that convey the story’s teaching or meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural pacing and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: First Nations storytelling involves... natural pacing of the telling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow for natural pauses, rhythm, and timing; patience and trust are essential for preparing to listen — pacing should support visualization and emotional response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic recall and fidelity
rubrics_metrics.description: Careful authentic recall of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect the integrity of the story by recalling and retelling it authentically; avoid altering culturally significant elements without guidance from knowledge-keepers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listening preparation and environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Patience and trust are essential for preparing to listen to stories. Listening involves more than just using the auditory sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a listening environment that fosters patience and trust; prepare listeners with prompts or framing that help them visualize and emotionally engage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storytelling as holistic learning and relationship-building
rubrics_metrics.description: First Nations storytelling is a foundation for holistic learning, relationship building, and experiential learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use storytelling not only to convey facts but to build relationships, cultural identity, and experiential learning opportunities; embed storytelling within broader community and learning practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptation for classroom use and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Teaching Storytelling in the Classroom. Download the Story Teller Worksheet to help you plan a learning activity for students to participate in story telling. Explore resources such as Circle of Stories (PBS) and Our Voices, Our Stories (Library and Archives Canada).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use provided resources and lesson-plan tools (e.g., Story Teller Worksheet) to adapt stories for classrooms; compare stories across Indigenous groups, consider the 'story blanket' concept for planning activities, and use multimedia resources where appropriate.
